authorizations.description: Signs a fresh RS256 JWT locally before every request, using a private key you control. Register the matching public key with Neon as a custom auth provider's JWKS URL. This avoids depending on a third-party auth provider and never hits an external token endpoint.
authorizations.name: custom

properties.description: PKCS#8 PEM-encoded RSA private key, e.g. generated with "openssl genpkey -algorithm RSA -pkeyopt rsa_keygen_bits:2048".
properties.label: Private Key
properties.name: privateKey

properties.description: Value for the JWT's "sub" claim. Row-Level Security policies typically use this via auth.user_id(), so it must match what your policies expect.
properties.label: Subject
properties.name: subject

properties.description: Value for the JWT header's "kid" claim. Must match the key id used in the JWKS document you publish for Neon to pick the right public key.
properties.label: Key Id
properties.name: keyId

properties.description: Optional value for the JWT's "aud" claim.
properties.label: Audience
properties.name: audience

properties.description: How long each freshly signed token is valid for.
properties.label: Expiration (Seconds)
properties.name: expirationSeconds

authorizations.title: Self-Signed JWT

properties.description: A JWT bearer token issued by your Neon Auth provider. Session JWTs typically expire after about 15 minutes, so this option is best for quick testing rather than scheduled workflows.
properties.label: JWT Token
